label: June 2026 paper — gap-fill practice variants (booklet Q1–Q50)

items.stem: A and B are 6 × 6 matrices with rank(A) = 4 and rank(B) = 5. Which of the following is a possible value of rank(AB)?
items.explanation: Sylvester's inequality gives rank(A) + rank(B) − n ≤ rank(AB) ≤ min{rank(A), rank(B)}, i.e. 3 ≤ rank(AB) ≤ 4. Only 3 lies in that range. Trap: rank(AB) can never exceed the smaller rank, and adding the ranks overshoots.

items.stem: A and B are 7 × 7 matrices with nullity υ(A) = 2 and υ(B) = 3. Which of the following is a possible value of υ(AB)?
items.explanation: For square matrices, max{υ(A), υ(B)} ≤ υ(AB) ≤ υ(A) + υ(B) (equivalent to Sylvester's rank inequality), i.e. 3 ≤ υ(AB) ≤ 5. Only 5 lies in that range. Trap: the nullity of a product is at least the larger nullity, never the smaller.

items.stem: X is a 10 × 3 matrix of rank 3 and P = Iₙ − X(X′X)⁻¹X′. The trace of P is
items.explanation: P is symmetric and idempotent, with n − k = 7 eigenvalues equal to 1 and k = 3 equal to 0, so tr(P) = n − k = 7. Trap: X(X′X)⁻¹X′ has trace k; subtracting it from Iₙ leaves n − k.

items.stem: Arrange the following statements of an R programme in the correct order to make a valid program. A. > y <- x * 2  B. > sum(y)  C. > x <- c(2, 3)  D. [1] 10  Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: x must exist before y is computed from it, y before it is summed, and the printed output comes last: C (x <- c(2, 3)), A (y = (4, 6)), B (sum(y)), D ([1] 10). Trap: an output line can only follow the command that produces it. (Output confirmed in R 4.5.1.)

items.stem: 3 coins are tossed 80 times with observed frequencies of 0, 1, 2, 3 heads equal to 12, 25, 33, 10. Assuming the coins are unbiased, the χ² goodness-of-fit statistic is (to three decimals)
items.explanation: Under fairness the number of heads is Binomial(3, 1/2) with probabilities 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8, so the expected frequencies are 10, 30, 30, 10. χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E = 4/10 + 25/30 + 9/30 + 0/10 = 1.533. Trap: dividing by the observed instead of the expected frequencies gives 1.606.
